parts.label: Nonzero relative mirror phase
parts.help: Show why reflected and transmitted amplitudes cannot have the same phase. The source defines phi as their relative phase. This proof is self-review.

parts.label: Relative phase magnitude
parts.help: Enter the magnitude in radians, using the official reflected-versus-transmitted phase convention. pi/2 is accepted.

parts.label: Returning pulse energy
parts.help: Use intensity reflectivity R, not amplitude reflectivity. Enter the leading high-reflectivity result. The exact ideal abrupt-switch result is also accepted.

parts.label: Energy-envelope decay time
parts.help: Use the leading energy-envelope e-folding time. The exact round-trip logarithmic time is also accepted. Other stated pulse-duration conventions require self-review.

parts.label: Pulse-duration convention
parts.help: State whether your duration refers to the energy envelope, amplitude envelope or another width. A different justified convention must be compared with the source rather than treated as an automatically wrong estimate.
